source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A mild cutaneous allergic reaction that can be observed first because hoarseness and throat tightness do not indicate airway involvement.","B":"Impending upper-airway compromise from anaphylaxis, requiring immediate intramuscular epinephrine and rapid airway assessment.","C":"An isolated anxiety response that can be treated with reassurance before any medication is considered for the allergic reaction.","D":"A delayed gastrointestinal manifestation of allergy that is unlikely to progress to respiratory or cardiovascular compromise."}}
source_row.rationale: Hoarseness and throat tightness in the context of an allergic reaction are concerning early signs of laryngeal edema and impending airway obstruction, a life-threatening feature of anaphylaxis. This requires immediate intervention, including prompt epinephrine administration (the first-line treatment) and preparation for possible advanced airway management if the airway continues to compromise.
source_row.source_detail: WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020, diagnostic criteria Table 2 and acute-management section: laryngeal symptoms and IM epinephrine first-line. 2020 guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
